A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VoxEval, with matching benchmark construction and retained experiments. All 13 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v3, including figures, tables, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of five SLMs across audio conditions, knowledge domains, and mathematics, including Tables 3–5, Figure 2, and response examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical evaluations and adds modality, chain-of-thought, input-length, and answer-extraction results in Tables 6 and 8.

M1.justification: v3 adds an inference variant using spoken chain-of-thought demonstrations containing intermediate reasoning steps; v1 evaluates direct-answer prompting only. The core MMLU-to-speech construction, augmentation pipeline, and evaluated model architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 6 adds speech-to-text and text-to-speech test scenarios for SPIRIT-LM, alongside speech-to-speech and text-to-text evaluation. The 56 knowledge subjects, mathematics subjects, six voices, and original audio variations are retained; newly stated dataset counts do not establish expanded data coverage.

E2.justification: The five evaluated SLMs remain unchanged. However, v1 Tables 3–4 include underlying text-LM reference comparisons involving Llama-7B, Llama-2-7B, Helium-7B, and GLM-4-9B; the corresponding rows are removed from v3 Tables 5 and 7.

E3.justification: The original five-shot, 80-second, Whisper-plus-string-matching setup is retained. v3 introduces CoT experiments using three dev-set demonstrations, compares 80-second truncation against untrimmed inputs, and adds GPT-4o answer extraction alongside string matching for mathematics. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v3 adds modality sensitivity analysis in Table 6 and tests CoT prompting, input truncation, and extraction sensitivity in Table 8. Appendix D adds an extraction-error case explaining accidental string-matching credit. The original audio-condition robustness plots and response examples are retained.

E5.justification: New Appendix B states that each experiment is performed once; v1 supplies no run count. This is newly disclosed information, not evidence of changed repetition counts. Neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests; Figure 2's subject-level variation plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: Retained overall, grouped, and direct-answer mathematics scores are numerically equivalent after percentage conversion. v3 adds SPIRIT-LM results of 23.77% speech-to-text, 1.38% text-to-speech, and 17.77% text-to-text, plus extensive CoT/extraction results, including TWIST's zero accuracy across all three untrimmed-CoT mathematics subjects. Text-LM reference scores are removed.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results or proofs. v3 Algorithm 1 expresses the existing maximum-score-difference calculation as pseudocode; the accompanying Figure 2 plots are identical. This documents existing analysis rather than introducing new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain speech-only knowledge evaluation, robustness across audio conditions, and spoken mathematics assessment. v3's introduction additionally presents CoT prompts as a benchmark capability for evaluating step-by-step reasoning, modestly extending the stated contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations concerning modality inconsistency, CoT effectiveness, input-length sensitivity, and accidental string-matching credit. New Section 6 identifies excluded evaluation dimensions and limits generalization from the single-model modality experiment. The retained GLM-4-Voice response example also gains a qualification that its explanation may be inaccurate.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the dataset-release promise with reported availability and a repository link. Appendix B supplies model sizes, SPIRIT-LM's base variant, single-RTX-A6000 hardware, and default-hyperparameter information. Dataset counts, random linguistic-variant selection, plotting pseudocode, and the GPT-4o extraction prompt are also newly documented.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wei et al. (2022), a benchmark-feature comparison in Table 2, and a more explicit breadth comparison with VoiceBench. Most related work is retained. Replacing the OpenAI citation with Hurst et al. updates the same GPT-4o system card rather than adding distinct research.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten around existing-benchmark limitations and the spoken-mathematics challenge. Several results paragraphs and the conclusion are rewritten, the stability discussion is consolidated, and the appendix organization expands. These changes extend beyond terminology and isolated copyediting.

P2.justification: v3 adds statistics, benchmark-comparison, and modality tables, Algorithm 1, and the extraction-prompt Figure 5. The mathematics table becomes a multi-block comparison with two extraction columns per subject, and the main accuracy table becomes single-column with text-LM rows removed. Figure 2's plots and Figures 3–4's prompts are retained.

improvement.justification: The modality and prompting analyses, extraction-error discussion, and access and implementation details make v3 more informative and reproducible. These gains outweigh the loss of text-LM reference comparisons, but the broad CoT conclusion needs qualification: Table 8 reports GLM-4-Voice elementary-math accuracy of 25.66% with direct answers and 27.25% with cut CoT, while SpeechGPT remains at zero. The disclosed single-run evaluation also limits the strength of the new conclusions.
